glosses: Having the faculty of sensation; pertaining to the senses.

examples.text: The sensitive faculty most part overrules reason, the soul is carried hoodwinked, and the understanding captive like a beast.

glosses: Responsive to stimuli.

examples.text: The engine seemed a little sensitive to wet rails, and in consequence the uphill work was not so good north of Dundee as it had been earlier. glosses: Easily offended, upset, or hurt.

examples.text: Max is very sensitive; he cried today because of the bad news.

glosses: Capable of offending, upsetting, or hurting.

examples.text: Religion is often a sensitive topic of discussion and should be avoided when dealing with foreign business associates.

glosses: Meant to be concealed or kept secret.

examples.text: These are highly sensitive documents.

glosses: Being aware of the feelings of others and taking care not to offend them.

examples.text: Thank you for being sensitive.

glosses: Important, intricate, and requiring great delicacy.

examples.text: The president's untimely statement disrupted some very sensitive negotiations.

examples.text: Her voice was barely perceptible over the noise, but her gestures made her meaning clear.

examples.text: The dismissal of a player who left Arsenal for Manchester City before joining Tottenham gave the home players and fans a noticeable lift.

glosses: Worthy of note; significant.

examples.text: Even in an era when individuality in dress is a cult, his clothes were noticeable. He was wearing a hard hat of the low round kind favoured by hunting men, and with it a black duffle-coat lined with white.

a significant look

glosses: Having a noticeable or major effect.

examples.text: That was a significant step in the right direction.
The First World War was a significant event.

The “little green men”—faces covered, wearing unmarked olive uniforms, speaking Russian and using Russian weapons—have played a significant role in both the occupation of Crimea and the civil war in eastern Ukraine.¹⁹⁶

glosses: Reasonably large in number or amount.
Having a covert or hidden meaning.
Having a low probability of occurring by chance (for example, having high correlation and thus likely to be related).

examples.text: In dumb significants proclaim your thoughts.

examples.text: For many people, the benefits of exercise in improving mood and preventing achiness are appreciable.

examples.text: A small hernia was just barely appreciable upon palpation.

translations.source_sense_description: (Sens figuré) En parlant des impressions morales

glosses: Having the faculty of sensation; pertaining to the senses.

examples.text: The sensitive faculty most part overrules reason, the soul is carried hoodwinked, and the understanding captive like a beast.

glosses: Responsive to stimuli.

examples.text: The engine seemed a little sensitive to wet rails, and in consequence the uphill work was not so good north of Dundee as it had been earlier. But I have noted this same "touchiness" on the part of the "A4s", and other modern British 4-6-2s, so that in this respect No. 2006 proved no exception.

glosses: Easily offended, upset, or hurt.

examples.text: Max is very sensitive; he cried today because of the bad news.

glosses: Capable of offending, upsetting, or hurting.

examples.text: Religion is often a sensitive topic of discussion and should be avoided when dealing with foreign business associates.

glosses: Meant to be concealed or kept secret.

examples.text: These are highly sensitive documents.
Xeltan: I cannot speak more about this problem; it is too sensitive. Suffice it to say, she has compromised my authority as a diplomat.

glosses: Being aware of the feelings of others and taking care not to offend them.

examples.text: Thank you for being sensitive.

glosses: Important, intricate, and requiring great delicacy.

examples.text: The president's untimely statement disrupted some very sensitive negotiations.

glosses: Accurate; able to register small changes in some property.
Having paranormal abilities that can be controlled through mesmerism.
A person with a paranormal sensitivity to something that most cannot perceive.

examples.text: [I]t is quite certain that many of their fears were unfounded, and centred upon perfectly innocent people - especially those who were what we now call "mediumistic" or "sensitives".
After all, Madame Rosita was a sensitive.
Swedenborg was one of the leading savants of Europe; it would be absurd to place any of our sensitives on the same intellectual level.
